title: What a model learned versus what you supply

sections.skill: Tell built-in knowledge from supplied or retrieved information

questions.prompt: What is a training cutoff?

choices.text: The date after which the training data has no information
The time limit for typing a question
The point where a model stops answering for the day
The maximum number of users at once

questions.correct_answer: The date after which the training data has no information
questions.intro: A model's built-in knowledge comes from its training data, which stops at a TRAINING CUTOFF date. It does not know about events after that date unless the information is SUPPLIED or RETRIEVED during your request: you paste a document, or the product runs a web search and adds the results to the context. These are different: built-in knowledge is patterns frozen at training time and may be incomplete or wrong, while supplied or retrieved text is current material the model reads now, which is only as good as its source. When an answer depends on recent facts, know which kind you are getting.
questions.feedback: Built-in knowledge stops at the cutoff.

sections.skill: Compare an encyclopedia on the shelf with today's newspaper

questions.prompt: The encyclopedia is like which kind of information?

choices.text: Retrieved information
Built-in knowledge
A web search
Neither kind

questions.correct_answer: Built-in knowledge
questions.intro: A printed ENCYCLOPEDIA on a shelf holds a lot of knowledge, but only up to the year it was printed. It cannot tell you yesterday's news. If you also hand someone TODAY'S NEWSPAPER, they can read current events, but the newspaper might contain mistakes, and it does not change the encyclopedia. A model's built-in knowledge is like the encyclopedia: fixed at its training cutoff. Supplied or retrieved text is like the newspaper: current material read right now.

sections.title: Apply it

sections.skill: Untangle blended answers about recent facts

questions.prompt: An answer quotes a supplied article correctly but adds a detail the article does not contain. Where might that detail have come from?

choices.text: Older built-in knowledge or an invented guess
The supplied article, which must contain it
A law that requires extra details
A permanent update to the model

questions.correct_answer: Older built-in knowledge or an invented guess
questions.intro: Answers often blend both kinds of information, and it is not always obvious which part came from where. A model might quote a supplied article correctly but fill a gap with older built-in knowledge, or describe a "latest" product that has since been replaced. Retrieved sources can also be outdated, unreliable or off-topic. Useful habits: ask the answer to say which statements come from the supplied material, check the dates of any sources, and confirm time-sensitive facts such as prices, laws, schedules and officials directly.
